newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian Cement Company falls on hard times.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian Cement Company falls on hard times.

text.p: Lack of funds and obsolete equipment have forced output to drop to five percent at Nigerian Cement Company (NIGERCEM), the company's chairman S.N. Anyanwu said at the weekend.

He told reporters on tour of the company's factory in the eastern Nigerian town of Nkalagu that to avoid a total closure the company had resorted to selling stock of various items lying idle in the stores and purchased in the 1960s and 1970s.
"Our technology is now obsolete. The cost of production and maintenance are high and we even lack the finance to purchase new spare parts," Anyanwu said.
"We have devised various means of surviving. We want to sell some unserviceable stock in the store valued at $1.8 million and lease out the quarrying factory at Ngbo."

NIGERCEM, founded in 1957 and wholly-owned by Nigerian shareholders as well as the federal and eastern states governments, is one of about half a dozen cement-producing companies in the West African country.

Others are Cement Company of Northen Nigeria, Ashaka Cement Company in the northeast, Ewekoro Cement Factory in the southwest, Okene Cement Company in the midwest and Benue Cement Company in central Nigeria.
Anyanwu said a monthly expenditure of about 23 million naira ($287,500) required to run the company had made it increasingly impossible to keep operations going.
He said the company planned to rehabilitate its production process at a cost of $127.8 million and when completed it would be able to produce 2,000 tonnes of cement daily.
The company had applied for loans from the Nigerian government agency Petroleum Trust Fund (PTF) and the African Development Bank (ADB) to enable it meet the rehabilitation costs, he said.
PTF was set up to rehabilitate delapidated public utilities with profits made from the 1994 four-fold petrol price hike.
Anyanwu said: "Already the ADB has agreed to participate in the rehabilitation and modernisation of our production through the setting up of a 'process line'."
